title: ASCEP Layer 5 — Application workload declaration
description: Layer 5 of the five ASCEP layers, mirroring ascep.capacity.Workload field-for-field. Turns a product question into a serving question: N concurrent sessions, M tokens/s. The highest-leverage input is avg_context_tokens — override the input + output/2 default whenever real conversation-length data exists.

application_type.description: Free-text application class (chat assistant, code completion, agentic loop, TTS feed, ...).

daily_active_users.description: Daily active users. Used with avg_session_seconds to derive peak concurrency via Little's law (peak_concurrent_users). Null permitted only when concurrent_users is set directly.

daily_active_users_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when daily_active_users is null (C1).

concurrent_users.description: Peak concurrent users, if known directly; overrides the Little's-law derivation. Units: users.

concurrent_users_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when concurrent_users is null (C1).

daily_users_tag.description: Provenance of the user figures (C2); forecasts are typically (U).

sessions_per_user_per_day.description: Sessions per user per day, dimensionless (Workload.sessions_per_user_per_day).

avg_session_seconds.description: Mean session wall-clock length, seconds. Pair with daily_active_users for Little's law. Null makes both peak_concurrent_users and demand_tok_s uncomputable from daily figures.

avg_session_seconds_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when avg_session_seconds is null (C1).

peak_to_mean.description: Peak-hour rate ÷ daily-average rate, dimensionless (Workload.peak_to_mean). 1.0 ('flat load') is almost never real; 3-6 is typical. Sizing to the mean with peak_to_mean=1 underprovisions by exactly this ratio.

duty_cycle.description: Fraction of a concurrent session actually generating, dimensionless (Workload.duty_cycle). capacity_at applies it to the KV floor but NOT to per-user token demand — applying it twice overprovisions by 1/duty_cycle, dropping it entirely underprovisions by the same.

input_tokens_per_request.description: Mean prompt tokens per request, tokens.

input_tokens_per_request_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when input_tokens_per_request is null (C1).

output_tokens_per_request.description: Mean generated tokens per request, tokens.

output_tokens_per_request_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when output_tokens_per_request is null (C1).

target_tok_s_per_user.description: Required per-stream generation rate, tokens/s (e.g. above reading speed, or enough to feed TTS without underrun). If null, demand is derived from session length instead.

target_tok_s_per_user_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when target_tok_s_per_user is null (C1).

peak_concurrent_users.description: Concurrent users at the peak hour (I), from Workload.peak_concurrent_users: (daily_active_users × sessions_per_user_per_day / 86400) × avg_session_seconds × peak_to_mean, or concurrent_users verbatim when that is declared. Every capacity floor is compared against THIS figure, so it MUST be stated rather than left implicit in the arithmetic.

peak_concurrent_users_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when peak_concurrent_users is null (C1).

active_sessions.description: Sessions holding a KV slot and generating at peak (I), from Workload.active_sessions: peak_concurrent_users × duty_cycle. Distinct from peak_concurrent_users by exactly the duty cycle; conflating the two mis-sizes the KV floor by 1/duty_cycle in whichever direction the mistake runs.

active_sessions_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when active_sessions is null (C1).

avg_context_tokens.description: Mean KV footprint per active session, tokens. Default (I): input_tokens_per_request + output_tokens_per_request/2 via Workload.avg_context_tokens. A real measured distribution SHOULD override the default; this is the highest-leverage input in the protocol.

avg_context_tokens_tag.description: Provenance of avg_context_tokens (C2); 'I' MUST name ascep.capacity.Workload.avg_context_tokens or the override method.

avg_context_tokens_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when avg_context_tokens is null (C1).

demand_tok_s.description: Aggregate output tokens/s required at peak (I), from Workload.demand_tok_s. The (I) claim MUST cite ascep.capacity.Workload.demand_tok_s.

demand_tok_s_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when demand_tok_s is null (C1).

application_type_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when application_type is null (C1).

daily_users_tag_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when daily_users_tag is null (C1).

sessions_per_user_per_day_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when sessions_per_user_per_day is null (C1).

peak_to_mean_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when peak_to_mean is null (C1).

duty_cycle_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when duty_cycle is null (C1).

requests_per_session_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when requests_per_session is null (C1).

avg_context_tokens_tag_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when avg_context_tokens_tag is null (C1).

images_per_request.description: Mean images per request, dimensionless. Feeds media_tokens_per_request; a workload that declares images in prose but leaves this null has no media term in avg_context_tokens, so the KV floor gets sized for text.

images_per_request_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when images_per_request is null (C1).

image_resolution_mix.description: Resolution distribution of declared images as {width, height, fraction} entries; fractions SHOULD sum to 1. On a dynamic-resolution model a single mean resolution hides a 10x token spread, so the mix is the declaration and the mean is not.

image_resolution_mix_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when image_resolution_mix is null (C1).

videos_per_request.description: Mean video clips per request, dimensionless. A value greater than 0 with a null video_seconds_per_request leaves the media term uncomputable, which is why the schema gates the two together.

videos_per_request_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when videos_per_request is null (C1).

video_seconds_per_request.description: Mean source clip duration per request, seconds. With video_sampling_fps it sets the frame count, and the frame count sets the media token term; null here makes videos_per_request unactionable.

video_seconds_per_request_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when video_seconds_per_request is null (C1).

video_sampling_fps.description: Frames sampled per second of source video that the APPLICATION requires, dimensionless. This is a declared sampling choice, not a property of the clip, and it is the single biggest lever on context length. The delivered value lives in serving media_preprocessing.video_sampling_fps; a disagreement between the two without a note means the report describes a workload the server did not run (addendum A1).

video_sampling_fps_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when video_sampling_fps is null (C1).

video_max_frames.description: Hard frame cap per request that the APPLICATION requires, frames. Null means unbounded, which means the context length is unbounded. The delivered cap lives in serving media_preprocessing.video_max_frames; a disagreement without a note means the report describes a workload the server did not run (addendum A1).

video_max_frames_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when video_max_frames is null (C1).

media_tokens_per_request.description: Total media expansion per request, tokens (M) from server-reported prompt_tokens on the real corpus or (I) from ascep.capacity.media_tokens_per_request, tagged inline as for peak_concurrent_users. This is the field that enters avg_context_tokens. 0 means measured and genuinely none; null means not reported. Conflating them turns an unmeasured workload into a text-only one, so the distinction is load-bearing.

media_tokens_per_request_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when media_tokens_per_request is null (C1).

reasoning_mode.description: Which mode the workload runs in. Thinking and non-thinking are two capacity profiles of one model, because reasoning tokens consume decode time and KV exactly like visible tokens; a single capacity number that does not name its mode is meaningless for a model that has both.

reasoning_mode_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when reasoning_mode is null (C1).

reasoning_share.description: Fraction of requests served in thinking mode, dimensionless in [0,1]. Only meaningful when reasoning_mode is mixed, and the schema requires it non-null there; under any other reasoning_mode it is noise.

reasoning_share_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when reasoning_share is null (C1).

reasoning_tokens_per_request.description: Mean reasoning tokens per request, tokens (M) from the server's usage fields or (I) from a named estimator, tagged inline as for peak_concurrent_users. 0 means measured-and-none; null means the server did not report it. Reasoning tokens are frequently not returned in the response content, so a harness counting visible characters under-counts output by the entire reasoning volume.

reasoning_tokens_per_request_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when reasoning_tokens_per_request is null (C1).

max_output_tokens.description: Output token cap per request, tokens. Under thinking or mixed mode the traces expand to fill whatever budget they are given, so a mean output length reported without the cap that produced it is not reproducible: the number describes the harness as much as the model (addendum A3). Required and non-null when reasoning_mode is thinking or mixed.

max_output_tokens_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when max_output_tokens is null (C1).

notes.description: Free-form prose keyed by field name, recording why a declared non-null value is what it is: that an input length is one observed datapoint rather than a fleet average. Complements the (U) mechanism, which can only justify a null; before this object existed, authors wrote value-justifications into _u_reason fields beside values that were not null, which is the abuse it replaces. A note NEVER substitutes for a value, never satisfies C1 beside a null, and is not evidence: it changes no tier and no conformance grade.
